answer: Sybil resistance needs every agent identity to cost a verified per-instance resource. Each agent posts a stake bound to a distinct runtime, slashed when two identities share one. It is a garden gate: it opens only after the deposit clears, and a duplicate root blocks the second key without refund. A thousand clones need a thousand live deposits all epoch, turning the swarm into a working capital bill on the wharf, not a free multiplier. Honest agents reclaim the stake at exit and pay only idle carry, so cloning is a balance sheet and the saffron reward count fades under sublinear payout caps.
